canonical_claim: For smooth regular surfaces S and T in Euclidean three-space, every smooth local isometry f from S to T preserves Gaussian curvature pointwise: K_T(f(p)) = K_S(p) for every p in the domain of f.
domain_and_universes: Smooth regular two-dimensional surfaces embedded in Euclidean R^3; points p on the source surface; universe and concrete Lean types remain open.
quantifiers: S, T: smooth regular surfaces in Euclidean three-space
f: smooth local isometry from S to T
p: point in the domain of f
hypotheses: S and T are smooth regular surfaces with their induced first fundamental forms
f is a local isometry at p
conclusion: GaussianCurvature T (f p) = GaussianCurvature S p
excluded_degenerate_cases: singular parametrizations or nonregular surface points
maps that preserve only area, angles, or topology rather than the full first fundamental form
mean curvature, principal curvatures separately, and other extrinsic invariants
the converse assertion that equal Gaussian curvature produces a local isometry

alternate_encodings.target: For two regular parametrizations with identical coefficient functions E, F, G, their Gaussian-curvature functions agree.
alternate_encodings.status: candidate only; transport must be checked in the statement phase

alternate_encodings.target: The extrinsic Gaussian curvature of an immersed surface equals the intrinsic sectional curvature of its induced metric.
alternate_encodings.relationship: stronger bridge formulation implying local-isometry invariance
alternate_encodings.status: candidate only; not a substitute for the canonical root

ambiguities_deferred_to_statement_phase: immersed versus embedded surface representation in Lean
minimal differentiability class supported by the selected curvature API
local isometry as a bundled map versus equality or pullback of metric tensors
coordinate formula and intrinsic sectional-curvature bridge declarations
